routes.name: Bear Harbor & Eel River Railroad (Bear Harbor Lumber Co. → Southern Humboldt Lumber Co.)
routes.gauge: CONTRADICTION — report both: (a) STANDARD gauge: NRHP nomination Section 8 ('a 2.0-mile-long standard gauge and cable railway', drawing on Bordon 1964 Western Railroader); Mendocino Beacon 12 Dec 1896 ('plans... to build standard gauge railroad'); North Coast Journal (Rohde, 'The Bear Harbor Railroad, 1892-1905'): '2 miles of standard-gauge track north from the wharf', Gypsy locomotives built to 4 ft 8 1/2 in. (b) NARROW gauge: same NRHP nomination Section 7 archaeology — site CA-MEN-2149H is 'remains of a narrow-gauge rail line' with Feature 1 'in situ, partially buried narrow-gauge tracks' matching the Douohor 1901 survey; and the CSP 1977 Bear Harbor-Usal inventory found 'a roadbed with narrow gauge and standard gauge rails throughout the area'. Do not resolve silently — the government document contradicts itself between its history and its archaeology sections.
routes.years: Built 1892-93 (locomotive No. 1 delivered by steamer 1892; line to Moody with incline completed June 1893); extended 1.5 mi down Indian Creek 1895 and 3.0 mi toward the Eel 1898; Bear Harbor & Eel River Railroad Co. incorporated Sept 1896; Moody→Andersonia extension built 1903-05 under Southern Humboldt Lumber Co.; 18 Apr 1906 earthquake wrecked mill/dam/track, mill never opened; last shipment from Bear Harbor 1907; rails/locomotives abandoned, dismantled 1921

sources: /Users/aodhan/vault/07 Files/Raw/lumber-ports/bear-harbor-landing-nrhp-nomination.pdf (NRHP draft, Bear Harbor Landing Historical and Archaeological District, read in full: §7 pp.4-20, §8 pp.21-50)
routes.notes: TOTAL LENGTH: 17.5 mi (NRHP §7) / 'nearly 18 miles of track ran from Bear Harbor wharf to Andersonia' by fall 1905 (NCJ 22 Nov 2018, quoted in NRHP). INCLINE: three readings — 1,900 ft (archaeological Feature 1, MEN-2149H), 2,000 ft (NRHP §7-8 narrative), 'pushed out 3,000 feet' Aug 1898 (Fort Bragg Advocate 17 Aug 1898); 600-ft rise; 3-rail gravity type with passing loop midway; loaded cars down hauled empties up; horses worked the 2-mile coastal stretch below. LOCOMOTIVES: No. 1 = 1892 Marschutz & Cantrell 0-4-0 'Gypsy' type (NRHP miscalls it a 'Shay'; NCJ: one of ~20 Gypsies built in SF 1882-92); No. 2 = Baldwin 2-4-2T, 1898; both preserved at Fort Humboldt SHP (Wikipedia). Route engineering: dozens of trestles (many >300 ft) and a 200-ft tunnel through solid rock (NCJ quoted in NRHP §8 p.48). Piercy (GNIS 1659386: 39.96626,-123.79532) lies across the SF Eel from Andersonia — context only, not on the line. Douohor's 1901 survey has the line running north from the pier then turning NW along 'Bear Harbor Creek'; the MEN-2149H site record says ENE along Bear Harbor Creek then north — drainage naming differs between accounts; the modern park name for the NW drainage the railbed follows is Railroad Creek. Railroad depicted on charts as late as 1941 (NRHP).

gaps: KEY OPEN ITEMS AND HONESTY FLAGS. (1) BEAR HARBOR GAUGE: the contradiction is real and internal to the NRHP nomination itself — Section 8 history (via Bordon 1964 and 1896 press) says STANDARD gauge and the surviving Gypsy/Baldwin locomotives are described as standard, but Section 7 archaeology records CA-MEN-2149H as a NARROW-gauge rail line with in-situ narrow-gauge track, and the 1977 CSP inventory found BOTH narrow- and standard-gauge rails on the ground. Both readings are reported in the route record; do not collapse them. A read of Bordon 1964 (Western Railroader No. 292) would be the next step. (2) BH&ER incline geometry: the top is well anchored (NHD Anderson Creek headwater tip 158 m from OSM Usal Road, matching the NRHP verbal), but the base coordinate [39.9378,-123.9502] is a bearing-derived offset — conjectural; the incline length itself has three source readings (1,900 / 2,000 / 3,000 ft). (3) SCHOOL MARM: GNIS 1724375 'School Marm Grove' (Woods) is at 39.88988,-123.91587, beside Wheeler and Jackass Creek ~2.7 km SSE of Bear Harbor — on the Lost Coast Trail corridor and the 1950s Wheeler mill area, NOT on the BH&ER alignment, and no consulted source names it as a railroad station; recommend NOT mapping it on this line.
